notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. The occasions of revelation (who the persons were, what happened) are not in the verses; they appear only under unknowns and uncertainties, as later tradition, with the hadith to add later. Pronouns the Arabic leaves open are left open. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: God has heard the speech of the woman who disputes with the one addressed about her husband and complains to God.
God hears the exchange that took place, for God is hearing and seeing.

Of those among them who make this declaration about their wives, God says that the wives are not their mothers, that their mothers are only those who bore them, and that they say an objectionable word and a falsehood.

chapters.summary_md: God says that He has heard the speech of the woman who disputes with the one addressed about her husband and complains to God [c1]. God hears the exchange, and is hearing and seeing [c2]. Of those who make this declaration about their wives, He says that the wives are not their mothers [c3], and that God is pardoning and forgiving [c4].
chapters.body_md:
God has heard the speech of the woman who disputes with the one addressed about her husband and complains to God [c1]. God hears the exchange that took place, for God is hearing and seeing [c2].

Of those among them who make this declaration about their wives, God says that the wives are not their mothers, that their mothers are only those who bore them, and that they say an objectionable word and a falsehood [c3]. God is pardoning and forgiving [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The first verse says what God has heard and that He is hearing and seeing [c1][c2]. The woman is not named and her words are not given [c1]. The verse at 58:2 speaks of a declaration by men about their wives, and names it by the Arabic verb yuzahirun; the verse does not spell out the words of the declaration [c3]. It ends with God's names pardoning and forgiving [c4].
chapters.kids_md: God says that He has heard the woman who disputes about her husband and complains to Him [c1]. God hears and sees everything that is said [c2]. God is pardoning and forgiving [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage begins with God hearing a complaint made to Him [c1][c2]. Another is that it calls an objectionable word an objectionable word, and ends with pardon and forgiveness [c3][c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the woman is, who her husband is, what she said, or when and where it happened. The verse says 'the woman who disputes' and names no one.
- Not established: who the one addressed is. The verse says 'you' and does not name him.
- Not established: what the declaration of 58:2 consisted of in words. The verb is yuzahirun and the verse does not spell it out.
- This chapter does not restate 58:3-4, which set out what follows for those who make the declaration. They are left to a scholar to present or not, in the verses' own words; the draft states no judgement on them.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the woman, of her husband, and the occasion. None is used in the story texts.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the occasion of these ayat, on who the woman was and on what was said, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.

The verses 58:3-4 are inside the inventory refs but are not drafted: they set out provisions for those who made the declaration, and the draft leaves any statement of them to a scholar. This is reported, not hidden.
